best_known_lineage.reason: Best measured task behavior in the campaign: 577/600 = 96.2% pooled research success across two disjoint panels and 196/200 = 98.0% on the task-reference panel, with the residual failures localized to one angular sector reproducible by an independent evaluator.

code.reason: Keep the full official 0.06-0.20 m training target radius range. The experiment shows the residual folded-branch deficit is not a coverage artifact (19 of 23 failures persist across independently fine-tuned weights, ten at radii both recipes trained on), so the range change neither causes nor cures the deficit, and no measurable harm was observed (all three policies within 0.34 points; at most 3 discordant episodes of 600). Aligning the training distribution with the official task removes a known train/deploy mismatch and is the correct standing base for the next investigation, whereas reverting would reintroduce a mismatch without scientific benefit.

last_lineage_decision.reason: The full-range fine-tune did not improve task behavior: on the fresh shared 600-episode panel (seed 22000) the parent working policy (experiment-2 checkpoint-100352) scored 580/600 = 96.67%, versus 579/600 = 96.50% for checkpoint-120832 and 578/600 = 96.33% for checkpoint-105472, and the parent won both paired comparisons (2 vs 1 and 3 vs 1 discordant episodes). The failure set was near-identical across all three (19 of 23 union failures common to all; at most 3 discordant episodes of 600), so no experiment-3 checkpoint demonstrates an advantage over the working policy. The working lineage remains the best-measured policy in the campaign (96.2% pooled research over 600 earlier episodes), and no fine-tuned checkpoint warrants replacing it. The residual deficit persists in the shoulder-limit folded-branch sector across the full radius range, so this experiment does not justify terminal assessment; request_final_benchmark is false.
